rounds.proof_sketch: size=262144, num_blocks=257, block_size=256. Block 255's last thread has idx=262140, satisfying idx+3<size (262143<262144), so main path handles elements 0-262143. Block 256 enters else branch with idx>=262144, but elem_idx>=262144>=size makes both original (elem_idx<size) and mutated (elem_idx<size-1) guards FALSE. No writes occur in else branch.
rounds.survival_reason: The fixed input shape [16, 16384] has exactly 262144 elements. With 257 blocks of 256 threads, the vectorized kernel's main path (condition idx+3 < size) processes all valid elements through block 255. Block 256 threads enter the else branch but have idx values starting at 262144, making elem_idx >= size. The original guard 'elem_idx < size' is already false for all these elements, so changing it to 'elem_idx < size - 1' has no effect. The mutation is in dead code for this specific tensor size.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape contract. The mutation affects code that is unreachable because the tensor size (262144) allows the vectorized main path to handle all elements completely. The else branch only activates for threads with out-of-bounds indices.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing on GPU kernels should verify branch reachability based on actual tensor sizes. For vectorized kernels, test with sizes that are NOT perfectly aligned to the vector width (e.g., 262145 elements = 262144 + 1) to ensure fallback/remainder paths are exercised.
